verdict.summary: Nice raised-floor timber base with a lantern and maple, but the roof is a heavy stacked-square lid with no curved, upturned eaves, and the paper-screen walls barely read.

issues.problem: Roof is concentric stepped squares (a ziggurat lid) with no hipped-and-gabled form and no upturned eaves; only tiny corner posts hint at curves. It dominates the small body and looks flat and heavy.
issues.fix: Rebuild with `mcd roof --preset teahouse` in a dark tile palette so eaves sweep up at the corners, and add a gabled top section/finial; reduce the overhang depth.

issues.problem: The sliding paper-screen walls are mostly dark solid timber with only two thin glass slits; no white panels in frames, so the shoji read is lost. The back elevation is mostly blank.
issues.fix: Use the glazing brush to fill the wall bays with white panel grids in dark frames, and add `mcd paint` or surround for lattice framing; open the centre bay as a wide shoji door.

issues.problem: Engawa veranda is not legible: the wraparound deck is just a plank band with huge dark posts, and no railing or stepping access. Stepping stones are a few grey slabs in odd places.
issues.fix: Extend the plank deck as a clear veranda with railing brush and a step up; lay a curving line of stepping stones from the path to the deck edge.

issues.problem: Posts taper and lean oddly in the street view, and the stilted floor leaves a wide gap with thin stone footings, so the body feels squat under the oversized roof.
issues.fix: Make posts straight and consistent, thicken footings with plinth brush, and raise wall height a block to rebalance with the roof.

issues.problem: Maple is a plain cube blob that covers the side view, and the lantern is tiny and lost.
issues.fix: Shape the maple canopy with an irregular, layered crown set back from the house, and move the lantern beside the path with a clearer stone base.
